---
title: Secrets
description: The secrets lifecycle — local .env.* files synced to GitHub environment secrets with names-only output, plus rotation and pruning.
---

Secrets live in exactly **two places**: local `.env.<environment>` files (never
committed) and GitHub environment secrets (written only by `gh` from those
files). Git history, chat transcripts, and CI logs are never secret stores.

This page is the condensed operating summary; the model behind it — who may
hold a value, and why — is the [trust model](/docs/concepts/trust-model).
The full procedure — including
single-secret updates and troubleshooting — is
[`plugins/gtm-sandbox/skills/gtm-sandbox/references/secrets.md`](https://github.com/nika-loki/paydirt/blob/main/plugins/gtm-sandbox/skills/gtm-sandbox/references/secrets.md)
in the repo; the `/secrets-sync` command wraps the same flow for plugin users
(`plugins/gtm-sandbox/commands/secrets-sync.md`).

## Prerequisites

- The GitHub CLI installed (`brew install gh` on macOS) and `gh auth login` done.
- The three environments exist — `scripts/sync-secrets.sh` creates missing ones
  automatically, or create them via
  `gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/<name>`.

## One file per environment

```text
.env.development    # scratch / vendor sandbox credentials
.env.pilot          # real credentials, limited scope
.env.production     # real credentials, full scope
.env.example        # committed template — placeholders only
```

`.env.example` is the only one ever committed, and its values are literally
`replace-me`:

```ini
HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN=replace-me
CLAY_API_KEY=replace-me
CRON_SECRET=replace-me
```

`.gitignore` must contain:

```text
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
```

## Sync

`scripts/sync-secrets.sh` wraps `gh secret set --env-file`, turning each
`KEY=value` line into an environment secret named `KEY`:

```bash
scripts/sync-secrets.sh --dry-run          # names-only preview: added / updated / prunable
scripts/sync-secrets.sh                    # development + pilot + production
scripts/sync-secrets.sh --env pilot        # one environment
scripts/sync-secrets.sh --prune --yes      # also delete remote keys removed locally
```

Behavior worth knowing:

- Re-running a sync updates same-name secrets and adds new ones. **Removals
  only happen with `--prune`** — deliberately interactive, because pruning is
  the only destructive operation in the lifecycle.
- Rotation is: edit the local file, `--env <environment>` re-sync, redeploy.
  Never `gh secret set KEY` with a literal value typed from a chat transcript.
- GitHub never displays a secret value to anyone after it is set — the owner
  included.

## Using secrets in workflows

Only jobs that declare `environment:` can read that environment's secrets —
that declaration is the isolation boundary:

```yaml
jobs:
  run-gtm:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pilot          # unlocks this environment's secrets
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run workflow
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
          STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY }}
        run: ./scripts/run.sh
```

A job without `environment: pilot` simply cannot see those secrets, regardless
of who dispatched it.

## Hygiene

- Keep the pre-commit guard installed — it blocks `.env*` staging before it
  reaches history.
- Prefer vendor sandbox keys (developer-mode apps) for `development`, so a leak
  there is low-impact by construction.
- Add a secret scanner (for example gitleaks, `gitleaks detect --no-git --redact`)
  to CI as a second net.
